recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is; adding more prose would be redundant and could drift from current request/response terminology and Bundle invariants.
issue_request: FHIR-6332 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 FHIR-core Feed issue asking to clarify why history bundle entries were required to carry transaction details; the resolution asked for create/update differentiation and transaction-like history processing rationale with boundary limitations.
initial_application: The issue was applied in SVN revision 6411, represented in git as 696b360575967d922958bf43deb51be8af31541c, which changed source/http.html to describe history Bundles as transaction-like input for pub/sub-style replication and to say request details let subscribers distinguish creates from updates.
additional_context: Current FHIR source uses request/response terminology instead of the old transaction element name, and later Bundle invariants require request and response details for history entries. A recent FHIR-7933 reconciliation updated the same paragraph to align with those rules while preserving the FHIR-6332 rationale.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/http.html already explains that history Bundles can be processed as transaction or batch-like input for replication with transaction-boundary caveats, and that entry.request information lets subscriber systems distinguish newly created resources from updates.

related_jiras.note: Reconciled the same source/http.html history paragraph with current request/response requirements while preserving the create/update rationale.
Later clarified that request and response details are mandatory for history Bundles, shaping the current wording around the old transaction requirement.
Moved Bundle type entry requirements into current invariants, including the history request/response rule.
